title: Binary Numbers (Base Two)
seo_title: Binary Numbers – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count in base two; change base ten numbers to binary numbers and binary numbers to base ten; add and subtract binary numbers. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on binary numbers: base two place values, changing between base ten and base two, and adding and subtracting binary numbers. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Base two (binary) uses only the digits 0 and 1. Computers store numbers this way.
  • The place values double from the right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
  • To change to base ten, add the place values where there is a 1. To change to binary, divide by 2 again and again and read the remainders upwards.

Examples

Example

1101₂ to base ten

8 + 4 + 0 + 1

Answer: 13

Example

19 to binary

19 = 16 + 2 + 1

Answer: 10011₂

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading remainders from the topRead them from the bottom up.
Using 10s as place valuesBinary places are 1, 2, 4, 8, …, not 1, 10, 100.
Writing 1 + 1 = 2 in binary1 + 1 = 10₂: write 0 and carry 1.
